The symbolic-capital columns are ZAxtSchwert (hatchets/swords), ZDolch (daggers), and Zhausgr (house size); other variables represent copper/gold, amber, monuments, depots, sickles, axes/celts, monument size, and pottery. The file presents all 15 columns as nonmissing, but the capital-variable columns are strings with decimal commas, so they must be normalized and parsed numerically before analysis. The row sequence has repeated data over consecutive 100-year BCE labels (observed examples 4300, 4200, 4100, 4000); the exact grouping/interpretation of rows and remaining periods should be checked before analysis.

Proposed approach, pending approval: parse decimal-comma values; check chronology, duplicated/value-identical rows, and numeric conversion; establish the intended PCA input set from the capital columns (exclude BCE/group/color); treat each 100-year row/time point as an observation unless inspection indicates another intended aggregation; perform PCA per slice if each slice supplies enough independent information, otherwise distinguish PCA across all observations from PCA fit separately within each slice. ### 2. Researcher — next_task

Thank you. Before proceeding, clarify how the 39-row capital dataset is organized across BCE time slices: please inspect all BCE labels and row repetitions, and determine whether multiple independent observations are present within each 100-year slice. Then recommend a defensible PCA design for the stated question—especially whether PCA can meaningfully be fit per slice or should be fit across observations and summarized by slice. Do not run PCA or report component findings yet; note any remaining ambiguity that the files cannot resolve.

**Decision:** continue

**Review phase:** approach_review; **approach approved:** False

**Basis:** Repository inspection identified capital.csv as the relevant 39×15 dataset, with decimal-comma measurements requiring parsing, but the observation structure and intended meaning of repeated 100-year labels are unresolved. Per-slice PCA validity depends on that structure.

**Open objectives:** Resolve time-slice structure and observation units in capital.csv.; Select a defensible PCA design before computing components or findings.

**Agent reply (plan)**

Inspection of every capital.csv row shows 39 unique BCE labels, from 4300 to 500 in exact 100-year decrements, with exactly one row per label. There are no repeated BCE labels, and the full rows are not duplicated. Thus the dataset does not provide multiple independent observations within any single 100-year slice: each time slice has just one multivariate profile. There are 37 distinct profiles across the 39 rows (the first three profiles are identical despite their different BCE labels). The group/color categories are contiguous temporal labels, not replication within slices. Consequently, fitting PCA separately within each 100-year slice is not meaningful: one row cannot define within-slice covariance or a multi-observation score distribution. A defensible data-only design is a single PCA across the 39 chronological profiles, using the capital-variable columns (exclude BCE, group, color), then plot/describe each row's PC1 and PC2 scores against BCE and summarize those scores by 100-year slices only as individual points—not as within-slice distributions. The wording 'distribution across PC2' must therefore be interpreted as the trajectory/range of time-point scores across PC2, not a distribution among independent observations in each slice. Alternatively, if the question intends loading values rather than scores, loadings are global to a single pooled PCA and cannot vary by slice; report the three variables' PC1 and PC2 loadings plus the 39 projected scores over time, distinguishing the two quantities clearly.

Recommendation for any later analysis: parse the 12 measurement columns from decimal commas, fit pooled PCA on the 39 rows with a transparent choice of scaling, then summarize the symbolic variables' loadings and per-date PC scores. Since the columns are labeled Z values, covariance PCA is a plausible primary choice; correlation PCA after re-standardization is also defensible but answers a different weighting question. Scaling cannot be inferred conclusively from this CSV. Preserve BCE order and do not treat the many repeated values across adjacent centuries as independent within-slice replicates. For missingness, the CSV has no blank cells, but malformed or unparsable values should still be checked; this does not establish how an upstream workflow handled missing values. Align PC signs by a declared convention only for presentation; PCA signs are arbitrary, and independently fitted axes (not recommended here) could also swap/rotate when eigenvalues are close.

Remaining ambiguity: files and metadata do not reveal what 'PCA conducted ... in hundred-year time slices' refers to in the source analysis. It may mean plotting/aggregating one-time-point scores in bins, or a different underlying dataset with repeated case-level observations not staged here. Nor do they specify intended variable subset, scaling, or whether the requested 'values on PC1' means component loadings or row scores. No PCA was run and no component findings are reported.

**Shared evidence:**

Executed complete-row inspection of capital.csv: labels are all 4300, 4200, …, 500, each occurs once; duplicated full rows=0; measurement profiles distinct=37, with first three rows matching across all measurement fields. Thus no slice has more than one dated row.

**Assumptions:** Each CSV row is interpreted as one dated multivariate profile; metadata provides no case-level sampling unit.; 'Distribution across PC2' can be provisionally described as the temporal spread/path of the pooled PCA scores, but this interpretation requires caveat.

**Uncertainties:** Source wording may refer to another dataset/workflow with independent observations absent from staged files.; Question does not distinguish variable loadings from observation scores.; Intended feature set, scaling and missing-data handling cannot be recovered from the files.

### 3. Researcher — next_task

The row-level inspection resolves an important design constraint: with one dated profile per BCE century, PCA cannot be estimated independently within each 100-year slice. Please proceed with the main analysis using a single pooled PCA across the 39 chronological profiles and the 12 capital-variable columns, excluding BCE/group/color. Parse decimal-comma values and document the scaling choice; given the Z-valued inputs, use covariance PCA on the supplied measurements as the primary analysis, while noting this is an assumption because the source method is undocumented. Report the symbolic variables’ PC1 and PC2 loadings separately from the dated observations’ score trajectory, and describe PC2 distribution only as spread/trajectory of the 39 scores across dates, not within-slice replicate distributions. State the sign convention and caveat that signs are arbitrary. Check conversion/data diagnostics and report variance explained and the key loadings/scores needed to answer the question. Do not substitute interpolated time_series_data variables for capital.csv.

**Decision:** continue

**Review phase:** approach_review; **approach approved:** True

**Basis:** Repository inspection reports 39 unique BCE labels, one row at each 100-year interval, no duplicated full rows, and 37 distinct measurement profiles. Thus per-slice PCA is not estimable; pooled PCA permits global loadings and dated scores. Method details including scaling and intended meaning of 'values' remain undocumented, so the requested analysis should distinguish loadings from scores and declare assumptions.

**Open objectives:** Run a transparent pooled PCA on capital.csv and report diagnostics and variance explained.; Determine symbolic-capital variables’ PC1/PC2 loadings and the distribution/temporal trajectory of observation scores across PC2.; Provide a caveated, data-grounded hypothesis answering the original question.

**Agent reply (result)**

A single pooled covariance PCA was fit to the 39 chronological profiles in capital.csv, using all 12 capital-variable columns and excluding BCE, group, and color. Decimal commas were converted to decimal points, and the supplied measurements were centered but not re-standardized (covariance PCA). This is the requested primary analysis; it assumes the Z-valued input columns are already comparably scaled, because the source method is undocumented.

The symbolic variables all have positive PC1 loadings under the stated orientation: hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) +0.301, daggers (ZDolch) +0.279, and house size (Zhausgr) +0.228. Thus they point in a broadly common direction on PC1, with hatchets/swords and daggers somewhat stronger than house size; these are loadings, not dated observation scores. On PC2, house size has the strongest of the three positive loadings (+0.364); daggers are more modestly positive (+0.120), and hatchets/swords are near zero but positive (+0.067). Accordingly, in the pooled two-dimensional variable orientation, house size is more associated with PC2 than either weapon variable, while the two weapon variables are oriented much more along PC1 than PC2.

PC1 and PC2 explain 31.84% and 20.42% of total variance, respectively (52.26% combined). The 39 PC2 observation scores—not within-slice replicates—range from -3.788 to +2.414 (median +0.393; quartiles -0.807 and +0.891). In chronological order, PC2 is strongly negative at 4300–4100 BCE (-3.788; identical profiles), rises to positive values by 4000 BCE (+0.528) and reaches +2.040 at 3500 and +2.414 at 3200 BCE. Scores are mostly positive through the middle stretch, though they vary; they turn negative at 2100 BCE (-0.566), fluctuate around zero/positive up to 1100 BCE (+0.484), then are negative from 1000 through 500 BCE (-1.483 to -1.685 at the endpoint). This is a temporal trajectory across one profile per century, not a within-century score distribution.

Diagnostics: all 12 measurement columns converted to finite numeric values; zero missing values were present. The parsed range was -3.134 to 3.949. Across features, means are essentially zero and sample standard deviations are mostly near 1 (0.537 for ZSichel, about 0.987–1.001 for most others), consistent with but not proving prior Z-scaling. There are 37 distinct measurement profiles among 39 rows (two repeated profiles; the first three rows are identical). PCA sign convention for presentation: flip PC1, if needed, so ZAxtSchwert's loading is positive; flip PC2, if needed, so ZDolch's loading is positive. Both signs—and hence positive/negative descriptions—are mathematically arbitrary; all scores were flipped together with their corresponding loadings. The PCA is global across dates, so loadings do not vary by century.

Limitation: capital.csv has one row per 100-year BCE label, so it cannot support a separate PCA or replicate-level PC2 distribution within each century. The source does not specify exact scaling or whether its question refers to loadings or scores; this report presents the pooled-variable loadings separately from pooled-PCA dated scores. The repeated identical profiles can affect score ranges and are retained as supplied. No interpolated variables from time_series_data.csv were used.

**Shared evidence:**

Execution output confirms 39x15 input, 12 features, zero missing measurements, all finite after decimal-comma conversion, two repeated measurement profiles; PC1/PC2 explained variance ratios 0.3184079/0.2041838; symbolic loadings as reported. PC2 scores reported directly from pooled decomposition; extrema and key-date values include 4300–4100 BCE = -3.7878, 3200 BCE = +2.4137, 1100 BCE = +0.4838, and 500 BCE = -1.6845.

### 4. Researcher — conclude

In the pooled covariance PCA of the 39 dated profiles, the symbolic-capital variables all have positive PC1 loadings under the stated sign convention: hatchets/swords +0.301, daggers +0.279, and house size +0.228. On PC2, house size is more prominent (+0.364), while daggers (+0.120) and hatchets/swords (+0.067) are comparatively weak. The dated PC2 scores range from about −3.79 to +2.41: strongly negative at 4300–4100 BCE, generally positive through much of the middle period, and negative again in the latest centuries. Because there is one profile per century, this is a temporal path of pooled-PCA scores, not a within-slice distribution. PC1 and PC2 explain about 31.8% and 20.4% of variance. PCA axis signs are arbitrary, and the covariance-PCA scaling choice is an assumption because the source method is undocumented.

**Decision:** stop

**Review phase:** result_review; **approach approved:** False

**Basis:** The reported analysis followed the agreed pooled design: parsed decimal-comma inputs, used all 12 capital variables while excluding date/group/color, checked numeric conversion and missingness, and distinguished global loadings from dated scores. Reported loadings, variance explained, and PC2 score range directly address the question, with the one-profile-per-century limitation stated.

decimal=' ,' semantics applied explicitly.\nXdf = df[features].replace({',': '.'}, regex=True).astype(float)\nX = Xdf.to_numpy()\nif not np.isfinite(X).all():\n    raise ValueError('Non-finite converted measurement')\n# Covariance PCA: center variables, do not scale/re-standardize them.\npca = PCA(n_components=2, svd_solver='full')\nscores = pca.fit_transform(X)\n# sklearn components rows are unit eigenvectors; columns are feature loadings.\nloadings = pd.DataFrame(pca.components_.T, index=features, columns=['PC1_loading','PC2_loading'])\nscore_df = pd.DataFrame({'BCE': pd.to_numeric(df.BCE), 'group': df.group,\n                         'PC1_score': scores[:,0], 'PC2_score': scores[:,1]})\nprint('shape',df.shape,'features',len(features),'missing input',df[features].isna().sum().sum())\nprint('numeric conversion: all finite',np.isfinite(X).all(),'range',X.min(),X.max())\nprint('identical measurement profiles',df[features].duplicated().sum())\nprint('feature means/std(ddof=1):')\nprint(Xdf.agg(['mean','std']).to_string())\nprint('explained variance ratio',pca.explained_variance_ratio_.tolist())\nprint('eigenvalues',pca.explained_variance_.tolist())\nprint('sign convention: orient PC1 so ZAxtSchwert loading > 0; orient PC2 so ZDolch loading > 0')\n# Apply declared presentation convention to both loadings and corresponding scores.\nfor comp, anchor in [(0,'ZAxtSchwert'),(1,'ZDolch')]:\n    if loadings.iloc[features.index(anchor),comp] < 0:\n        loadings.iloc[:,comp] *= -1\n        scores[:,comp] *= -1\nloadings = pd.DataFrame(pca.components_.T, index=features, columns=['PC1_loading','PC2_loading'])\nfor comp, anchor in [(0,'ZAxtSchwert'),(1,'ZDolch')]:\n    if loadings.iloc[features.index(anchor),comp] < 0:\n        loadings.iloc[:,comp] *= -1\n        scores[:,comp] *= -1\nscore_df['PC1_score'] = scores[:,0]\nscore_df['PC2_score'] = scores[:,1]\nprint('symbolic loadings:')\nprint(loadings.loc[['Zhausgr','ZDolch','ZAxtSchwert']].to_string())\nprint('all loadings:')\nprint(loadings.to_string())\nprint('scores sorted chronologically BCE descending:')\nprint(score_df.to_string(index=False,formatters={'PC1_score':'{:.4f}'.format,'PC2_score':'{:.4f}'.format}))\nprint('score range/mean/sd:')\nprint(score_df[['PC1_score','PC2_score']].agg(['min','max','mean','std']).to_string())\nprint('PC2 score quantiles:')\nprint(score_df.PC2_score.quantile([0,.25,.5,.75,1]).to_string())\n# Save reusable transparent outputs.\nloadings.to_csv('/workspace/capital_pca_loadings.csv')\nscore_df.to_csv('/workspace/capital_pca_scores.csv',index=False)\nPY\npython /workspace/pca_capital_analysis.py",
